title: Canon disclaimer string pinned verbatim in 4 files across 3 packages
evidence:
server/src/application/application_detail_handler.gleam:1058:const written_response_disclaimer = "Written response, provenance-checked. Not verbally confirmed. A quick call to the referee is the strongest final check."
server/test/application/application_detail_handler_test.gleam:351:    "Written response, provenance-checked. Not verbally confirmed. A quick call to the referee is the strongest final check.",
shared/test/reference_call_test.gleam:360:        "Written response, provenance-checked. Not verbally confirmed. A quick call to the referee is the strongest final check.",
client/test/components/reference_panel_test.gleam:799:        "Written response, provenance-checked. Not verbally confirmed. A quick call to the referee is the strongest final check.",
detail: Every future wording change must be edited 4 ways across shared/server/client tests. This follows the repo's pinned-copy convention, but the propagation cost is structural — each #612-style rewording repeats the ripple.
recommended_fix: Keep the exact pin server-side only; relax cross-package pins to prefix matches, as reference_detail_payload_integration_test.gleam:139 already does ("Written response, provenance-checked").

title: Lint boundary is scope-enumerated for server code — new user-facing server modules silently escape coverage
evidence:
CLIENT_GLOB = "client/src/**/*.gleam"
SERVER_INCLUDE = [
    "server/src/copy.gleam",
    "server/src/application/application_detail_handler.gleam",
---
            <> " landlord send(s) failed — see per-landlord Sentry events",
detail: Client is globbed wholesale; server user-facing modules are a hand-maintained include list. The #612 boundary ("user-facing modules are dash-free, period") holds only while every new public-prose module is manually added.
recommended_fix: Glob server/src with an explicit exclusion list for developer-facing modules (e.g., digest_handler, sms_client) instead of an include list, so new user-facing modules are covered by default.
